summary_paragraph: A man with a history of COPD, prior stroke, coronary artery disease with bypass, hypothyroidism, and alcohol abuse was admitted for a two-day history of left lower extremity swelling, redness, and warmth concerning for cellulitis. He was wheelchair-bound and had dry, flaky skin with fungal infection of the toes, increasing infection risk. Initial evaluation showed no deep vein thrombosis on Doppler ultrasound but revealed a Baker’s cyst. He had no systemic signs of infection, and labs showed normal white blood cell count and mild hyperkalemia. He received IV vancomycin and Unasyn, with significant clinical improvement. He was discharged home on oral Bactrim and cephalexin for continued coverage, along with clotrimazole cream for dermatophytosis. His chronic conditions were stable and managed with home medications, including Plavix, inhalers, gabapentin, and levothyroxine. Iron was switched to ferrous gluconate to reduce constipation. He was advised to follow up with his primary care provider and return if symptoms worsened.
